props.statement: Comparing feeds of CO + H2 (1), CO2 + H2 (2) and a mixture (3): feed 1 gives few by-products (95 % methanol) and low refining costs, has a heat of reaction ΔH = -21.630 cal./mol. (as printed), a large chance of hot spots in the catalyst, and needs a CO2 absorber; feed 2 gives more by-products and much water and higher refining costs, with ΔH = -11.850 cal./mol. (as printed), no hot spots, and needs a selective oxidation of CO; feed 3 gives more by-products and some water (80 % methanol), its heat depends on the CO : CO2 ratio and a good ratio prevents hot spots; desulfurization of the feed gases is always required.
